args: Analyze the reentrancy vulnerability around obj_hash_code(), h_check_modified(), AR-to-HT conversion, ht_init()/ib_init(), and user-defined key.hash callbacks in src/hash.c. Which state fields must be snapshotted and checked to reliably detect structural mutation, and are there other callback dispatch sites using the same guard? Recommend a minimal root-cause patch preserving behavior.

The reported ASan crash is a heap-use-after-free in mrb_byte_hash_step via mrb_str_hash_m, called from obj_hash_code at src/hash.c around line 345 while ar_set converts a 16-entry AR hash to HT for a 17th insertion. A user key's Ruby hash callback mutates the same Hash during index rebuilding. The current h_check_modified reportedly compares representation flags, table/EA pointers, and capacity but omits logical size and ea_n_used, allowing same-allocation insert/delete mutation to evade detection. I have not yet patched anything; I am examining the exact structs and guard call sites to choose between extending the snapshot/check and preventing callbacks during partial construction.
